name: United States
note: Hybrid is an accepted interim step; the end state is pure PQC.
applies_to: Specified US federal-agency systems. National security systems are excluded from EO 14412 and are governed separately by NSA CNSA 2.0. Private-sector organisations are not bound by either.
regulatory_urgency_basis: CNSA 2.0 mandates, FedRAMP, FIPS 140-3, OMB M-23-02

name: Canada
note: CCCS roadmap ITSM.40.001 allows hybrid as a transitional stage; high-priority systems by 2031, full migration to pure PQC by 2035.
applies_to: Government of Canada systems, via the CCCS migration roadmap.

name: Brazil
regulatory_urgency_basis: ITI/ICP-Brasil PQC study group, early stage

name: European Union
note: The EU coordinated implementation roadmap (NIS Cooperation Group PQC workstream, June 2025) recommends standardised, tested hybrid solutions whenever feasible and suitable. Quantum-vulnerable public-key mechanisms must not be used on their own after the end of 2030 for high-risk use cases, and after the end of 2035 for medium-risk ones. By 2035 the transition should be completed for as many systems as practically feasible. The roadmap states no end state: it does not say whether hybrid is later retired.
applies_to: EU-level coordinated implementation roadmap addressed to member states; member states implement nationally.

name: United Kingdom
note: Hybrid is acceptable as an interim; NCSC prefers a pure-PQC end state.
applies_to: Staged migration targets published as NCSC guidance for UK organisations; not a single binding cut-off date.

name: France
note: ANSSI strongly recommends hybrid wherever post-quantum protection is deployed, in the short and medium term; hash-based signatures (SLH-DSA, XMSS, LMS) are the exception. Its PQC guidance has, to date, no regulatory force by itself; hybrid is mandatory inside the regulated scope (classified and Diffusion Restreinte data, vital-infrastructure systems, ANSSI product qualification), where ANSSI aims to add PQC requirements for qualification from 2027.
applies_to: ANSSI PQC FAQ and security-visa qualification requirements; applies to products seeking French qualification.
regulatory_urgency_basis: ANSSI 2025 PQC readiness mandate, hybrid TLS requirement

name: Germany
note: BSI TR-02102-1 recommends quantum-safe key agreement and signatures only in hybrid form with classical mechanisms; hash-based signatures may in principle be used alone. The guideline itself is a recommendation; BSI says other BSI documents are binding for certain applications.
applies_to: BSI TR-02102-1 technical guideline: a recommendation; other BSI documents are binding for certain applications.
regulatory_urgency_basis: BSI TR-02102 PQC guidance, NIS2 transposition

name: India
note: DST/NQM National Quantum Mission roadmap (2023) and CERT-In guidelines mandate PQC adoption for Critical Information Infrastructure by 2027 and full nationwide adoption by 2033. Published guidance aligns with NIST standards toward pure PQC; no explicit hybrid requirement published.
applies_to: Critical Information Infrastructure operators, via the DST/National Quantum Mission quantum-safe roadmap; CERT-In BOM guidelines cover CBOM/QBOM reporting. A national roadmap with dated milestones rather than a binding cut-off for all organisations.
regulatory_urgency_basis: DSCI/CERT-In PQC awareness, no formal mandate yet
